skill.name: latency-tracker
skill.description: Per-call and aggregated latency tracking for MEV infrastructure. Use when implementing performance monitoring or debugging slow operations. Triggers on: latency, timing, performance, slow, speed, instrumentation.
skill.summary: Guides span-based latency tracking, aggregation, and alert thresholds for MEV infrastructure.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive from a markdown TypeScript code fence in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only documentation for latency instrumentation and does not execute shell commands or request sensitive data.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 42 opens a TypeScript markdown code block, not a shell or Ruby backtick expression. The fenced example documents tracker.span usage and contains no command execution path.

content.user_title: Track MEV Latency With Span Guidance
content.value_statement: Latency issues in MEV systems are hard to isolate across calls and transaction stages. This skill guides span hierarchy, instrumentation, aggregation, and alert thresholds.
actual_capabilities: Defines a span hierarchy from end-to-end flow to individual calls.
Guides wrapping operations in tracker span calls for timing.
Suggests alert thresholds for hot path, RPC, and submit latency.
Supports debugging slow operations through structured latency data.
Frames latency tracking for MEV infrastructure workflows.
limitations: It does not include a runnable latency tracking library.
It does not collect metrics or store telemetry by itself.
Threshold values are examples and need calibration for each system.
It focuses on MEV infrastructure rather than general product analytics.

use_cases.title: Instrument MEV Execution Paths
use_cases.description: Add spans around Rust calls, RPC calls, transaction submission, and confirmation steps.

use_cases.title: Investigate Slow Operations
use_cases.description: Map slow paths to named spans so repeated latency spikes are easier to compare.

use_cases.title: Define Latency Alerts
use_cases.description: Create threshold guidance for hot path, RPC, and end-to-end submit timings.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Spans
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latency-tracker skill to propose a span hierarchy for my MEV workflow with Rust calls, RPC calls, and transaction submission.

prompt_templates.title: Instrument a Slow Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Add timing to an existing operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latency-tracker skill to show where I should add timing spans in this slow MEV operation and explain each span name.

prompt_templates.title: Set Alert Thresholds
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latency-tracker skill to recommend alert thresholds for Rust hot path calls, RPC calls, and end-to-end submit latency.

prompt_templates.title: Design Aggregated Reporting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latency-tracker skill to design an aggregated latency report across spans, percentiles, success status, and operation names.

output_examples.input: Plan latency tracking for a liquidation workflow.
output: Child spans: Rust hot path call, RPC eth call, transaction submit, and transaction confirmation.
Report success status and total elapsed time for each completed flow.

output_examples.input: Suggest alerts for slow RPC calls.
output: Track RPC latency as a named child span.
Use a warning level near the expected upper range.
Raise an alert when calls exceed the documented example threshold.

output_examples.output: The plan should name each span clearly, keep the root flow visible, and separate Rust, RPC, submit, and confirmation timing.

best_practices: Use stable span names so metrics can be compared over time.
Record both per-call timing and the full end-to-end flow.
Calibrate alert thresholds with production baseline measurements.
anti_patterns: Do not track only total duration when child operations can hide spikes.
Do not mix unrelated operations under one vague span name.
Do not copy example thresholds without checking real workload behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill run performance tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for designing latency spans and alert thresholds.

faq.question: Can it help with MEV transaction timing?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on MEV flow timing from hot path calls through transaction confirmation.

faq.question: Does it require a specific metrics backend?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is backend-neutral and can be adapted to common observability tools.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the alert thresholds production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are examples and should be tuned against real latency baselines.

faq.question: What is the main output of the skill?
faq.answer: It helps create a span hierarchy, instrumentation plan, and alert threshold recommendations.
